faqLeft.q: What engine does the Mercedes GLE500e use?
faqLeft.a: The GLE500e uses the M276 — a 3.0-litre V6 petrol engine — with an electric motor for its plug-in hybrid system. It was fitted to the W166 generation from 2016 to 2018.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes GLE500e engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £3,200. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my GLE500e?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm your exact M276 PHEV spec before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild M276 GLE500e engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We rebuild M276 petrol engines from the GLE500e as standard, using OEM-spec components for timing chains, bearings, and gaskets.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used GLE500e engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my GLE500e if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does a GLE500e engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most GLE500e owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
